headline: Van Gerwen survives two match darts to edge Coates
standfirst: The three-time Grand Slam champion ended a run of three straight opening-match defeats on TV with a deciding-leg win over a 20-year-old debutant.
body: Michael van Gerwen came within a dart of another early setback before beating Henry Coates 5-4 in Group L of the Grand Slam of Darts on Saturday.
Coates, 20 and making his debut at the event, had two darts to win the match while Van Gerwen waited on 56. He missed both, and the Dutchman checked out to take the deciding leg.

The win ended a frustrating sequence for Van Gerwen, who had lost his first match at each of his previous three televised tournaments. Only one player from his group reaches the knockout stage, so the early points could prove valuable.
The match was one of the best of the opening night, with nine maximums between the two players.

Van Gerwen had spoken before the tournament about his recent weight loss and his determination not to slip back into old habits. After the match he described the last spell as one of the toughest of his life, but said he was relishing the fight, according to Dartsnews.
